headline: A shallow M7.7 earthquake struck the Azuero Peninsula at 12:56 local time. SINAPROC's first official communiqué reports no deaths, no missing persons and some injured, with damage across six provinces.
key_points: Official (SINAPROC Communiqué No. 1): no deaths, no missing persons; some injured, incl. 15 students with minor injuries in Coclé.
Worst documented damage: Penonomé (partial hotel collapse, churches, facades) and southern Azuero (homes collapsed in Los Santos).
Fire stations damaged in six provinces; much of the Soná station collapsed, trapping emergency vehicles.
Water treatment plants damaged nationwide; Chilibre plant serving Panama City at 20% capacity.
Damage also reported in Chiriquí, the Pearl Islands and Darién; Tonosí and Pedasí hospitals lightly damaged.
Strong aftershocks continue: 47+ recorded (IGC-UP), largest M6.6 near Coiba at 15:25 local.

areas.text: Partial collapse of Hotel Dos Continentes; San Juan Bautista cathedral tower fell onto a car; Gobernación wall collapsed; market damaged (1 injured); Hospital Aquilino Tejeira cracked and evacuated; Iguana Mall damaged.
Described as the most affected area by Telemetro; partial collapse of a hotel and adjoining houses; road damage. Closest towns to the epicentre; strongest modelled shaking (MMI VIII–IX).
El Sitio hostel collapsed. Locals told La Prensa people were trapped, but local authorities say the damaged tourist buildings in Pedasí were unoccupied. No official confirmation of anyone trapped.
Cathedral and municipal building damaged (partial roof collapse); bus terminal and Policlínica Horacio Díaz Gómez damaged.
Soná fire station damaged; road to Torio (Mariato) split with vertical offsets; Santiago–Arenas road cut. M6.6 aftershock at 20:25 UTC centred 14 km W of Río Grande (Soná).
Part of the Basílica Menor tower collapsed.

areas.area: Chitré, Los Pozos, Las Minas & La Villa, Herrera/Los Santos
areas.text: SINAPROC reports damage in Chitré (no details); cracked homes in Las Minas; in La Villa de Los Santos the San Atanasio church bell tower cracked and the Museo de la Nacionalidad roof and stairs were damaged. Few images yet — information gap.
Ceiling collapse in a school/university building (Telemundo video). Sunday Guardian, citing Telemetro, reports significant damage to at least six buildings — unconfirmed.
Broken windows on Calle 50 and Paitilla; hospitals evacuated as a precaution; Metro lines 1 and 2 suspended; Tocumen airport closed.
Considerable structural cracks at the Macaracas fire station (Fire Brigade via SINAPROC). Strong modelled shaking; few other reports so far.

Light damage to homes and businesses and to several schools in Chiriquí; cracks at the David fire station; shops and homes affected in the Pearl Islands; minor damage to a school in Darién (SINAPROC).

services.text: Distribution outages in six provinces (Chiriquí, Herrera, Los Santos, Veraguas, Coclé, part of Panamá Oeste); 17 circuits restored in Colón. ETESA says the national transmission network is stable.
Water treatment plants damaged nationwide (IDAAN); Chilibre plant, serving most of Panama City and San Miguelito, at 20% capacity.
Widespread mobile and internet failures across several operators.
Tocumen International closed and evacuated; flights diverted to Barranquilla, Cartagena, Bogotá, San José, Managua and Panamá Pacífico.
Road to Torio (Mariato) ruptured; Santiago–Arenas road cut; damage around Cambutal.
Operating normally; ACP denied rumours of damage to Agua Clara locks.
Classes suspended nationwide; University of Panama closed; public offices closed by presidential order.
PTWC initially warned of 1–3 m waves on Panama's coasts; later no Pacific-wide threat. No tsunami damage reported.
Panama City municipality suspended all municipal services, including markets, until further notice.

upcoming: Further official communiqués from SINAPROC / Ministry of Government expected; figures will be updated as they are published.
unknowns: Total number of injured — SINAPROC reports 'some people injured' without a national count.
How many homes are damaged or destroyed; Los Santos reports collapsed homes but no figures yet.
Damage in the hardest-shaken rural areas (Tonosí, Macaracas, Las Minas, Los Pozos), where reporting is limited.
Extent of damage to water treatment plants and when supply in Panama City will be restored.
Landslides in the hills of southern Azuero and Veraguas (modelled risk is high).
